description: Divergence class: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS). Object keys must sort by UTF-16 code unit at every nesting level. Pins exact canonical JSON and its base64url.
Divergence class: 48-byte / base64url encoding. A fixed 48-byte sequence (0x00..0x2f) must base64url-encode identically across SDKs (no padding, URL-safe alphabet).
Divergence class: base64url of a UTF-8 string. Pins the URL-safe, unpadded base64url of an ASCII label so every SDK's base64url helper agrees.

Divergence class: JCS key sort (RFC 8785 3.2.3). Keys must sort by UTF-16 code unit, NOT by Unicode code point / UTF-8 byte order. The astral key U+1F600 encodes in UTF-16 as the surrogate pair D83D DE00, so its FIRST code unit (0xD83D=55357) sorts BEFORE the BMP key U+FB03 (0xFB03=64259); under code-point/UTF-8 order U+1F600 (128512) sorts AFTER U+FB03, flipping the two keys. Any SDK that sorts by code point / raw UTF-8 bytes emits the astral key last and fails RED. Expected bytes computed per RFC 8785 with the JS reference (harness/src/conformance/jcs.ts), which is canonical.

Divergence class: JCS string escaping (RFC 8785 3.2.2.2). U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) are NOT in JSON's escape set (they are >= U+0020 and neither backslash nor quote), so canonical JSON MUST emit them as literal UTF-8 (E2 80 A8 / E2 80 A9), never as \u2028 / \u2029. Serializers that escape them for JS-embedding safety (legacy JSON.stringify polyfills, some PHP/JSON defaults) emit different bytes and fail RED. Expected bytes computed per RFC 8785 with the JS reference (jcs.ts), which is canonical.

Divergence class: JCS number canonicalization (RFC 8785 3.2.2.3 / ECMAScript Number-to-String). Non-normalized numeric literals must serialize to their shortest canonical form: 1.0 -> 1, 1E2 -> 100, 100.00 -> 100, 1.50 -> 1.5. An SDK whose JSON stack preserves the raw number token (Go json.Number, Python Decimal, arbitrary-precision decoders) re-emits 1.0/1E2/100.00 verbatim and fails RED. Expected bytes computed per RFC 8785 with the JS reference (jcs.ts), which is canonical.
